turn_clearance_m.description: Forward clearance (m) at which the corner turn begins; must stay strictly below direction_estimator.corner_clearance_m, enforced at load.

narrow_turn_clearance_m.description: Forward clearance (m) at which the corner turn begins when the corridor reads NARROW; must stay strictly below turn_clearance_m.

centering_gain_deg_per_m.description: Road-wheel steering degrees per metre of lateral offset; 0.0, because centring swings the heading past the direction alignment gate.

heading_gain.description: Road-wheel steering angle per unit of heading error against the corridor axis (dimensionless); the damping term centring lacks.

max_centering_steer_deg.description: Road-wheel degrees ceiling on the heading damping term; sized by stability, not geometry (corner branches use max_corner_steer_deg).

max_corner_steer_deg.description: Road-wheel degrees the corner-turn and back-off branches steer at; sized by geometry so the arc fits the branch's commit clearance.

steer_cap_from_commit_distance.description: Scale the corner steering cap by each branch's commit distance instead of applying max_corner_steer_deg to all branches.

corner_speed_scale.description: Fraction of creep speed while turning a corner blind. Slower than straight running, because the turn is committed on one comparison rather than a plan.

reverse_speed_scale.description: Fraction of creep speed while backing off a wall.

turn_arc_half_fov_deg.description: Half field-of-view (deg) of the wider arc used as a second opinion on whether the corridor has ended, checked before a hard-over turn.

turn_open_range_m.description: Longest valid forward return (m) over the turn arc at or above which the way ahead still counts as open, so the corner turn does not commit.

corner_leak_margin_m.description: Margin (m) added to WIDE giving the side range past which a side counts as opened, no longer a wall to centre against.

min_forward_clearance_m.description: Back off when the wall ahead is this close (m); defaults to the chassis length but is tunable independently.

min_reverse_clearance_m.description: Room needed behind (m) before backing off is allowed; defaults to the chassis length but is tunable independently.

bay_start_sector_deg.description: Half-angle (deg) of the sector whose MEDIAN range stands in for the single +/-90 deg ray in direction_from_parking_bay; 0.0 restores the single ray.

bay_start_max_checks.description: Scans the placement test may be retried over before it is given up for the round; 1 restores the tick-1-only test. Bounded so it cannot fire mid-creep at a corner.

bay_wall_clearance_m.description: Side clearance below which a start counts as boxed against the bay wall, for direction_from_parking_bay's wall-against-open test.

assume_bay_start.description: Begin an OBSTACLES round assuming the robot was placed inside the bay instead of waiting for the scan to prove it.

bay_exit_clearance_guard.description: Bound each exit leg by predicted fin clearance instead of contact; a contact-bounded leg-end is the 9.24.7 violation.

bay_exit_clearance_margin_m.description: Fin clearance (m) the guard refuses to go below.

bay_exit_guard_overlap_recovery.description: Let a leg that improves an already-violated fin gap run, so the guard does not veto motion away from the overlap.

bay_exit_guard_block_ticks.description: Unbroken ticks of the guard refusing both legs before handing over to the contact-bounded exits; 0 = never.

bay_exit_arc_steer_norm.description: Steering both guarded legs hold, as a fraction of full lock; a cliff at 1.0, with only ~2 deg of margin.

bay_exit_speed_scale.description: Extra speed scale on both guarded legs; a cliff: 1.0 never moves, 0.5 collides.

bay_exit_cycle.description: The legacy contact-bounded exits, reachable only with the clearance guard off. Kept configurable because which one a real chassis needs is unproven.

bay_exit_cycle_reverse_m.description: Distance (m) the legacy contact-bounded cycle exit reverses before switching back to a forward leg.

bay_exit_cycle_reverse_steer_norm.description: Steering held on the legacy cycle exit's reverse leg, as a fraction of full lock.

bay_exit_forward_m.description: Distance (m) the legacy contact-bounded cycle exit drives forward before switching back to a reverse leg.

bay_exit_reverse_m.description: Distance (m) the reverse-then-swing exit reverses before its forward leg begins.

bay_exit_steer_norm.description: Steering magnitude held on the reverse-then-swing exit's forward leg, as a fraction of full lock.

bay_exit_reverse_steer_norm.description: Opposite lock on the reverse leg -- REFUTED 2026-08-29. Held forward lock (bay_exit_hold_steer) is what makes the yaw cross and the ratchet bite.

bay_exit_hold_steer.description: Hold the forward leg's steering lock through the reverse leg, instead of re-commanding centre or opposite lock.

bay_exit_leg_stall_ticks.description: Ticks of no wheel travel that end a leg (1 is a cliff -- no leg ever runs).

bay_exit_latch_direction.description: Decide which side is open once, not every tick: once the chassis rotates, the +/-90 deg comparison is noise and a flip turns the escape into a re-entry.

bay_exit_open_side_sector_deg.description: Half-angle (deg) of the sector over which the open side is scored instead of a single ray; do not widen or it reaches the end walls.

bay_exit_open_side_votes.description: Ticks polled before latching the open side; 1 restores the old tick-1 latch.

bay_exit_latch_reverse.description: Latch the reverse leg done once its distance is covered, so the manoeuvre cannot chatter back into reverse.

bay_exit_fallback_frames.description: Ticks before switching to the other legacy exit / handing over; 0 = never.

bay_exit_max_frames.description: Hard bound (ticks) on the whole bay-exit manoeuvre; 0 = never, which can stall the round.

bay_exit_speed_mps.description: Absolute speed (m/s) for the bay-exit legs; 0 = keep the inherited scaling. A hardware number set above the motor deadband.

bay_exit_contact_dist_m.description: Forward clearance (m) below which the nose counts as touching a wall, triggering the straight reverse-off recovery.

bay_exit_contact_recovery_ticks.description: Ticks of nose-contact reverse-off recovery; ships disabled (0) because it reverses blind into a fin.

bay_exit_target_yaw_deg.description: Rotation (deg) from the placement heading at which the exit has turned enough to leave; in the pocket rotation is the only working signal.

bay_exit_leg_max_s.description: Cap the free-turn check of each exit leg by the longest measured leave-the-bay leg (s); 0 = unbounded.

bay_exit_guard_measured_coast.description: Budget the guard's stopping distance from measured wheel speed instead of commanded; inert pending a hardware trial.

bay_exit_clearance_tolerance_m.description: Predicted fin overlap (m) the guard tolerates; ships 0.0 (inert). Tolerating overlap risks fin contact.

bay_exit_guard_mirrors_reverse.description: Steer the opposite way on the reverse leg so the two arcs curve opposite ways and yaw accumulates instead of cancelling.

bay_exit_guard_reverse_straight.description: Back STRAIGHT on the guarded ratchet's reverse leg. The alternatives are measured and both cost: mirroring the lock buys rotation but pays a full lock-to-lock servo swing (1.23 s at servo_slew_rate_rad_s, against legs of about 0.3 s), while holding the lock is free and accumulates nothing, since at constant steering magnitude the lateral displacement is a state function of heading and a closed cycle returns both. A straight reverse keeps the heading the arc won and buys back the room it spent.

bay_exit_prime_steer.description: Hold the chassis still until the servo has swung to the FIRST leg's angle, the way every leg after the first is already budgeted by _begin_leg. The opening leg has always started from centred wheels and driven while the servo slewed: measured inside the pocket the wheel needs 0.62 s to reach lock at servo_slew_rate_rad_s, the chassis covers the pocket's 6.5 cm of along-wall slack in about that time, and the exit turns 1.3 degrees instead of the 8 its turn radius allows, so it reaches the fin ahead with the wheel still on its way.

bay_exit_dr_uses_measured_yaw.description: Dead reckon each bay-exit leg with measured yaw instead of the yaw its steering implies; refuted, ships false.
